Case_19011/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1: Photograph of the patient’s facial lesion upon presentation to the oncology clinic

description.short_caption: Facial lesion with extensive necrosis and crusting.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a large, necrotic lesion involving the left cheek and extending to the perioral region. The lesion is characterized by black eschar, crusting, and surrounding erythema. The tissue damage appears extensive, with irregular borders and significant involvement of the skin. The patient’s eyes are obscured for privacy, and the lesion is visibly severe, suggesting a possible infectious or neoplastic etiology.
visible_findings: large necrotic lesion on the left cheek

Case_19011/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 4: Photograph of the patient’s facial lesion six weeks after completion of therapy

description.short_caption: Facial lesion six weeks post-therapy, showing healing with residual scarring and erythema.
description.detailed_description: This composite image shows four views of the patient's face, highlighting a large lesion primarily involving the left cheek and extending to the chin. The lesion appears to be healing, with areas of erythema, scarring, and crusting visible. The surrounding skin shows mild discoloration and irregular texture. The images suggest improvement following therapy, though residual damage remains. The patient is seated in a clinical setting, and the photographs are de-identified with black bars over the eyes.
visible_findings: healing lesion on left cheek and chin

Case_19011/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Skin, H&E stain, 40X (Courtesy of Diana Basemera)

description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows skin tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 40X magnification. The epidermis is visible on the right, with keratinocytes arranged in layers. The dermis contains inflammatory infiltrates, including numerous mononuclear cells and scattered neutrophils. There is evidence of tissue remodeling and possible edema. The staining highlights cellular and extracellular components distinctly.
